newsitem.title: UK: Europe crude outlook - Sellers spoiled for choice.
newsitem.headline: Europe crude outlook - Sellers spoiled for choice.

text.p: Sellers of North Sea crudes may be spoiled for choice this week after refiners slurped up most available grades in a massive buying spree last week leaving the market tight and differentials sharply higher, traders said.
Dated Brent reversed a contango against forward paper after a U.K. major holding all but a handful of early October Brent cargoes discarded them gradually at increasingly higher levels.
For crude as a whole, gas oil will remain a crucial prop.
"While gas oil is still strong you're not going to see refinery throughputs come off," said a trader.
Dealers said they expected fundamentals to remain positive unless U.S. heating oil stocks made a surprising recovery.
Although the Brent/WTI arbitrage was still unworkable, traders thought U.S. demand for distillate-rich crude could open it up arb this week.
Some West African grades moved into the U.S. Gulf last week despite the steep backwardation.
Nigerian grades were said sold out, thanks to Med refiners starved of Russian Urals taking West African grades to make up for tight sour availibility.

India took three VLCCs of November-loading Qua Iboe in last week's tender, plus four cargoes of Dubai. But the IOC award masked an unworkable eastern arbitrage for African barrels, restricted to two VLCCs to Taiwan in October, traders said. Busy trade has cleared out all North Sea grades other than Brent for first decade October, while only seven cargoes remain for the second, said a trader for a major North Sea producer.
"There's still a few Ekofisks left, but that's a mogas crude...it's the distillates that everyone is interested in," said one trader.
"We're looking mainly at late October avails now. Both buyers and sellers have a reason to hold out until next week to see if things move their way," another trader said on Friday.
CFD's indicated Dated Brent values were likely to hold at a 10 cent premium to November paper but could move higher.
Norwegian Oseberg found seasonal strength on the back of strong gas oil and traded at a 40 cent premium to Dated Brent this week.
Oseberg and Gullfaks were sold out for the second decade, while just one cargo apiece of Statfjord and Forties were still up for grabs on Friday.

Mediterranean refiners were waiting for the full October Urals programme for predictions of where the sour market was heading. Sellers are already smacking their lips at the prospect of Dated -65 cents for October Urals.
